args: In ffmpeg/libavcodec/iff.c, what is the best root-cause validation strategy for negative AVCodecContext.bits_per_coded_sample affecting cmap_read_palette() and decode_init()? Is zero a meaningful/accepted value for this decoder, and are there other dangerous uses before cmap_read_palette() that justify rejecting negatives in decode_init() as well as validating cmap_read_palette()?

The reported ASan crash is a heap overflow at ffmpeg/libavcodec/iff.c:180 in cmap_read_palette's grayscale fallback. A fuzzer control block sets bits_per_coded_sample negative. decode_init at line 404 accepts all values <=8 and chooses PAL8 for values <8, while cmap_read_palette only rejects values >8 and performs multiple shifts by bits_per_coded_sample. I am considering either a narrow unsigned range check in cmap_read_palette, an early negative check in decode_init, or both. I want to preserve valid behavior and address all negative-value paths rather than only the observed palette overwrite. Current code also assigns the value to s->bpp and uses it in allocations/decoding.
